issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to a Milkable interface (and students are instructed to implement/use Milkable), but the solution repository defines an interface named Dairy (with messageOnMilk()) and also includes an empty Milkable.java. Classes in the solution implement Dairy (e.g., Goat, Seal) rather than Milkable. This name/type mismatch between Milkable vs. Dairy will confuse students about which interface to implement and compile against.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the interface name consistent across all artifacts. Rename the solution's Dairy interface to Milkable (or replace the empty Milkable.java with a proper Milkable interface) and have Seal and Goat implement Milkable. Ensure Milkable.java defines String messageOnMilk() and remove the unused/empty Milkable file or merge its contents so template, problem statement, and solution use the same interface name.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to an interface named 'Milkable' (the concept for animals that can be milked), but the solution implementation defines and uses an interface named 'Dairy' for the same concept. Additionally, the solution contains an empty Milkable.java file alongside Dairy.java, which increases confusion. This inconsistent naming between 'Milkable' (problem/template) and 'Dairy' (solution) can create cognitive mapping barriers for students trying to map the exercise requirements to the provided solution code.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the interface name across all artifacts. Rename Dairy.java and the interface declaration to Milkable (and update Goat, Seal, and other references to implement Milkable), or else update the problem statement and template to use 'Dairy' consistently. Alternatively, provide a non-empty Milkable interface that delegates to or extends Dairy to preserve both names temporarily, but preferred fix is a single consistent name: 'Milkable'.
